entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5545"/><title type="x-s2">PSALM 10</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Ps.10.1-Ps.10.18">Psa 10:1-18</reference>. The Psalmist mourns God's apparent indifference to his troubles, which are aggravated by the successful malice, blasphemy, pride, deceit, and profanity of the wicked. On the just and discriminating providence of God he relies for the destruction of their false security, and the defense of the needy.</title> <div sID="gen8418" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5545"/>1. These are, of course, figurative terms (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.7.6">Psa 7:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.13.1">13:1</reference>, &c.).<div eID="gen8418" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8419" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hidest--</hi>Supply "thine eyes" or "face." <div eID="gen8419" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: PSALM 10 Psa 10:1-18 . The Psalmist mourns God's apparent indifference to his troubles, which are aggravated by the successful malice, blasphemy, pride, deceit, and profanity of the wicked. On the just and discriminating providence of God he relies for the destruction of their false security, and the defense of the needy. 1. These are, of course, figurative terms (compare Psa 7:6 ; 13:1 , &c.). hidest-- Supply "thine eyes" or "face."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5549"/><div sID="gen8425" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5549"/>5-6. Such is his confidence in the permanence of his way or course of life, that he disregards God's providential government (out of sight, because he will not look, <reference osisRef="Isa.26.11">Is 26:11</reference>), sneers at his enemies, and boasts perpetual freedom from evil. <div eID="gen8425" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 5-6. Such is his confidence in the permanence of his way or course of life, that he disregards God's providential government (out of sight, because he will not look, Is 26:11 ), sneers at his enemies, and boasts perpetual freedom from evil.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5550"/><div sID="gen8426" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5550"/>7-10. The malignity and deceit (<reference osisRef="Ps.140.3">Psa 140:3</reference>) of such are followed by acts combining cunning, fraud, and violence (compare <reference osisRef="Prov.1.11">Pr 1:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.18">18</reference>), aptly illustrated by the habits of the lion, and of hunters taking their prey. "Poor," in <reference osisRef="Ps.10.8">Psa 10:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.10.14">10, 14</reference>, represents a word peculiar to this Psalm, meaning the sad or sorrowful; in <reference osisRef="Ps.10.9">Psa 10:9</reference>, as usual, it means the pious or meek sufferer. <div eID="gen8426" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7-10. The malignity and deceit ( Psa 140:3 ) of such are followed by acts combining cunning, fraud, and violence (compare Pr 1:11 , 18 ), aptly illustrated by the habits of the lion, and of hunters taking their prey. "Poor," in Psa 10:8 , 10, 14 , represents a word peculiar to this Psalm, meaning the sad or sorrowful; in Psa 10:9 , as usual, it means the pious or meek sufferer.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5555"/><div sID="gen8434" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5555"/>13-14. It is in vain to suppose God will overlook sin, however forbearing; for He carefully examines or beholds all wickedness, and will mark it by His providential (Thine hand) punishment. <div eID="gen8434" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5557"/><div sID="gen8437" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5557"/><hi type="bold">15. arm--</hi>power.<div eID="gen8437" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen8438" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">till thou find none--</hi>So far from not requiting (<reference osisRef="Ps.10.11">Psa 10:11</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.10.13">13</reference>), God will utterly destroy the wicked and his deeds (<reference osisRef="Ps.9.5">Psa 9:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.9.6">6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.34.16">34:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.37.36">37:36</reference>). <div eID="gen8438" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 15. arm-- power. till thou find none-- So far from not requiting ( Psa 10:11 , 13 ), God will utterly destroy the wicked and his deeds ( Psa 9:5 , 6 ; 34:16 ; 37:36 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv5558"/><div sID="gen8439" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv5558"/>16-18. God reigns. The wicked, if for a time successful, shall be cut off. He hears and confirms the hearts of His suffering people (<reference osisRef="Ps.112.7">Psa 112:7</reference>), executes justice for the feeble, and represses the pride and violence of conceited, though frail, men (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.9.16">Psa 9:16</reference>). <chapter eID="Ps.10"/>
